sources.locator: Paul Erdős, On the Sum and Difference of Squares of Primes (1937). Crossref record inspected (Erdős proved the case k = 2: the number of representations n = p^2 + q^2 is unbounded). Erdős Problem #979 page inspected. OEIS A385316 inspected: the smallest numbers with exactly 1, ..., 5 representations as sums of three prime cubes are 24, 185527, 8627527, 999979163 and 10588881419. A local enumeration of all prime triples with cube sum at most 10^10 confirmed that no N <= 10^10 has more than 4. For k = 3 and N <= 10^10 the maximum is 4, so the task recovers such an N.
